Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

Indian Standard 



( Reaffirmed 2005 ) 



IDENTIFICATION PAINTING AND INSCRIPTION 
CODE FOR PILOT CRAFT 



1. Scope — Prescribes unified colour diagrams of the outside painting and the identification marking 
of pilot croft to permit their identification in heavy weather. 

1.1 This standard applies to pilot craft used in closed waters estuaries and open roadsteads to bring 
and take off pilots to merchant ships. 

1.2 The applicability of requirements of this standard to pilot craft navigating under a navy fiag shall 
be determined by the competent authority. 

-2. Definition — The definitions given in IS : 10862-1984 Classification and basic requirements of pilot 
craft shall apply. 

3. Painting — In order to make the most effective use of the outside painting, the pilot craft shall be 
painted m the following two ways: 



a) Pilot craft with a freeboard amdships 
of 1 m and more 



b) Pilot craft with freeboard amidships 
less than 1 m 



Hull — yellow orange 

Superstructure/Deck House — White 

Hull and Superstructure/Deck house — yellow 
orange 



3,1 To paint the surfaces yellow-orange, paints of a light, saturated, pure yellow -orange tint shall be 
used. Red-orange tints are not permitted see IS : 5-1978 Colours for ready mixed paints and enamels. 



4. identification Inscriptions 

black colour. 



Pilot craft shall carry an identification inscription 'PILOT' in 



4.1 The inscription ' PILOT ' on pilot craft with a freeboard of 1 m or more shall be made on both sides 
of the hull ( see Fig. 1 ). The height of the letters shall be not less than half of the freeboard amidships. 
The locations of the inscription shall be determined by the competent authority. 




FIG. 1 PILOT CRAFT WITH A FREEBOARD OF 1 m OR MORE 

4.2 The inscription 'PILOT' on pilot craft with a freeboard of less than 1 m shall be made on the deck 
house walls or on special boards on the superstructure on both sides (see Fig. 2). The height of the 
letters shall be not less than 250 mm. 

For pilot boats the inscription may be made on the house roofs. If there is not enough space 
to place the word 'PILOT' on the house roof, a black circle with a letter ' P ' in white, the base 
pointing to the bow of the boat, may be used instead. 



Adopted 30 March 1984

FIG. 2 PILOT CRAFT WITH A FREEBOARD OF LESS THAN 1 m 

4.3 The location of the inscriptions on the hull superstructure and deck house as well as the dimensions 
of letters and signs and the length of the inscriptions shall be determined by the competent authority 
based on the requirements for maximum visibility and legibility of the inscription from a distance. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This Indian Standard has been formulated with an objective to improve the efficiency of pilot 
service and the safety of navigation in heavy weather. This standard is based on ISO 6217 
'Shipbuilding — Inland navigation — Pilot craft — Identification painting and inscriptions ' issued by 
International Organization for Standardization ( ISO ).
